BiblicalUsage: David went up by the ascent of Olivet, and wept as he went up, and had his head covered, and he went barefoot, and the Lord told Isaiah, go and loose the sackcloth from off thy loins, and put off thy shoe from thy foot.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe bare feet say what words cannot: David climbs Olivet weeping and barefoot as a mourner, and Isaiah walks barefoot as a sign, and in both cases the shoe comes off because the ground is holy or the grief is real.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
